title: Growing Together East zoning and Lawrence Avenue housing
subtitle: Also: regional economic development strategy endorsed, climate work plan approved, and industrial land conversion questions.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee recommended a new land use and zoning framework for three transit station areas in east Kitchener: Block Line, Fairway and Sportsworld. Known as Growing Together East, it sets the rules for how these areas can grow and is tied to the city's federal Housing Accelerator Fund commitments. The Official Plan part must also go to the province for approval {{vote:m4}}.

The committee also recommended allowing an 18-unit, three-storey rental apartment building at 288-292 Lawrence Avenue. This needs a change from industrial employment to low-rise residential designation {{vote:m3}}. Some councillors asked about keeping industrial land, and staff said that broader question is being studied in the new Official Plan.

The committee further recommended endorsing the 2025 Waterloo Region Economic Development Strategy {{vote:m2}} and approving the 2024-2026 Climate Change and Environment Committee work plan {{vote:m1}}. These are recommendations only. Council will make the final decisions at a later meeting.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the Official Plan amendment and approving two zoning by-law amendments for the Block Line, Fairway and Sportsworld transit station areas, with the Official Plan amendment forwarded to the province and the zoning taking effect only once the earlier Growing Together by-law is in force.
The committee recommended approving the Official Plan and zoning changes that would convert the site from industrial employment to low-rise residential for an 18-unit apartment building.
The committee recommended endorsing the 2025 Waterloo Region Economic Development Strategy to guide collaboration among municipal economic development partners.
The committee recommended approving the Climate Change and Environment Committee Work Plan for 2024-2026.

debate: On the economic development strategy, one councillor asked whether the 2015 agreement had clarified the roles of the city, the region and the regional economic development corporation. Staff said the roles are clear at a staff level and that a working group meeting twice a year can address any overlap.

A councillor asked about the type of housing being built, including more affordable starter homes and modular housing. Another noted the strategy flags a shortage of serviced industrial land, while this meeting was converting industrial land to housing. Staff asked that the question be held for the planning items.

On Lawrence Avenue, the applicant's planner said the corridor is already a mix of residential and light commercial uses, not typical employment land. Staff said the change is an intensification of an existing residential use. Councillors supported it, and some called for more flexible zoning.

Councillors asked whether the Lawrence Avenue building could include ground-floor space such as a daycare, a path to nearby Belmont Park, affordable units and renewable energy. The applicant's planner said non-residential uses are possible but not proposed, and a path may not be feasible because of lot shapes. No units are designated affordable, though the owner is pursuing federal rental financing with affordability requirements, and heat pumps are intended.

On Growing Together East, a councillor asked who set the station area boundaries. Staff said the Region set them in 2022. Asked about industrial land, staff said lands in these areas are not protected employment lands, and a wider employment land study is under way in the new Official Plan work.
